newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi airline carries 224,000 T cargo in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi airline carries 224,000 T cargo in 1996.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp carried 224,000 tonnes of cargo last year, up from 215,000 tonnes in 1995, a cargo official was quoted as saying on Monday.

The Saudi newspaper Okaz also quoted Omar Ashram, assistant general manager of cargo marketing, as saying the Middle East's biggest carrier expected to increase its share in the world air cargo market when it takes delivery of a new fleet of aircraft.
In 1995 the airline signed a deal worth more than $6 billion to buy 61 jets from Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

Ashram said the airline was planning to start regular cargo flights to Johannesburg, N'Djamena, Nairobi, Dakar and Kanu in Africa; Houston and Los Angeles in the United States; Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Dhaka, Madras, Lahore, Dehli and Seoul in Asia; and Dubai and Sharjah.
